items.basis: The claimed 1.7-1.8 V contribution from relativistic effects in PbO2 and PbSO4 is physically implausible; battery voltage arises from electrochemical potential differences, not relativistic effects, which are negligible at battery operating energies
The 15-year boundary condition without exceeding 2% antimony is unrealistic given the evidence showing that even low-antimony grids corrode significantly at float voltages above 2.25 V/cell

The candidate's evidence contradicts itself as [doi:10.1109/intlec.1995.498976] shows grid corrosion is the dominant failure mode in VRLA batteries at float voltages, yet the candidate claims to solve this with a mechanism that doesn't address the fundamental electrochemical corrosion process

The proposed solution offers no improvement over baseline as calcium-tin alloys without antimony have been commercially available for decades and are known to have inferior mechanical properties compared to traditional lead-antimony alloys

Reducing antimony below 2% while maintaining mechanical strength is impossible as documented in [doi:10.1016/s0378-7753(98)00028-7], which shows that low-antimony alloys require additional strengthening elements that increase hydrogen evolution

The testable prediction of <5% grid cross-section reduction after 15 years fails to account for localized corrosion at grain boundaries, which would cause premature failure despite average cross-section measurements appearing acceptable
